episodes.169895: An upper level low pressure system moved along the Canadian border throughout the day.  This feature dragged a cold front through Montana that set off multiple thunderstorms.  Some of the storms became severe and one generated a tornado that impacted the town of Glentana.
episodes.169940: A unseasonably strong mid-level disturbance (shortwave) moved across a weakly unstable airmass during the evening of July 18th. Scattered showers and a temporary embedded thunderstorm or two developed behind the main rain shield and moved across VT. This particular cell had no history of thunder but enough of an updraft tapped the strong mid-level wind field above to produce a weak EF-1 tornado that lasted only a few minutes at most.
episodes.169945: A thunderstorm produced locally heavy rain, in a short period of time, over an urban area prone to flash flooding.
episodes.170078: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed into northwestern Arkansas during the evening of the 17th, along a cold front that moved into the area. The strongest storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.170362: Deep southwesterly flow aloft developed in advance of a vigorous upper-level low leading to the development of storm activity, some severe, across much of the CWA, but particularly along the Hi-Line. Although some hail was produced, this was primarily a strong, gusty wind event.
episodes.170487: Scattered thunderstorms developed in the afternoon along the sea breeze, and a large cluster of storms moved over and offshore of Brevard County. These storms produced several strong wind gusts at the Cape.
episodes.170736: Short lines of thunderstorms moved east across the Mississippi River. The storms produced isolated wind damage before they weakened east of Interstate 57. The storms occurred along a cold front that extended from central Indiana southwest to the Ozark Mountains of Arkansas. A very moist and unstable air mass supported the storms over Missouri, where mixed-layer cape generally exceeded 2000 j/kg. Southwest 850 mb winds increased to over 30 knots, further aiding storm development. The storms weakened as they outran the more unstable air.
episodes.170738: Small clusters of thunderstorms organized into a line of thunderstorms that produced scattered pockets of wind damage across southeast Missouri, mainly along and north of U.S. Highway 60. The storms occurred along a cold front that extended from central Indiana southwest to the Ozark Mountains of Arkansas. A very moist and unstable air mass supported the storms over Missouri, where mixed-layer cape generally exceeded 2000 j/kg. Southwest 850 mb winds increased to over 30 knots, further aiding storm development.
episodes.170765: Several bands of thunderstorms containing damaging winds developed along a cold front.
episodes.170766: Several bands of thunderstorms containing damaging winds developed along a cold front.
episodes.170769: Several bands of thunderstorms containing damaging winds developed along a cold front.
episodes.170865: Several bands of thunderstorms containing gusty winds developed along a cold front.
episodes.170969: An area of storms developed along a frontal boundary to the north of the International Border during the early morning hours of the 18th. As these storms moved into northeastern Minnesota from Ontario, they were able to tap into some lingering instability and produce damaging wind gusts as they dropped to the south. Tree damage was reported along the path of this line of storms with most of the reports coming in later in the morning, well after the storms had passed.
episodes.171011: A low pressure system with a warm front pushed through Central New York, providing support for isolated storms. While instability was limited, there was enough to support one lone severe storm that knocked down a few trees in Steuben County.
episodes.171105: A storm moved into the eastern shore of Maryland and produced strong winds and some wind damage.
episodes.171167: A rather large and slow-moving area of thunderstorms moved east across the lower Ohio Valley. The storms produced heavy rainfall and isolated urban flooding. The storms occurred ahead of a cold front that extended from central Indiana southwest to the Ozark Mountains of Arkansas. A very moist and unstable air mass supported the storms. Southwest 850 mb winds increased to over 30 knots, further aiding storm development.
episodes.171168: A rather large and slow-moving area of thunderstorms moved east across the lower Ohio Valley. The storms produced heavy rainfall and isolated urban flooding. The storms occurred ahead of a cold front that extended from central Indiana southwest to the Ozark Mountains of Arkansas. A very moist and unstable air mass supported the storms. Southwest 850 mb winds increased to over 30 knots, further aiding storm development.
episodes.171190: Active weather remained in full force on July 18th as several rounds of showers and thunderstorms worked their way through West Virginia. The most impactful convection took place on the morning of the 18th, when downed trees resulted in damage to a residential trailer and flash flooding occurred in Cabell and Wayne Counties. Heavy rain also transpired in the afternoon the day prior, which led to high water issues in Putnam County.
episodes.171304: A low pressure center was parked over the northern half of Indiana throughout much of the day on the 17th, with points to the south, including KY, exhibiting a warming and moistening trend throughout the day. Scattered showers and storms were present across Kentucky and surrounding areas throughout the afternoon and evening. A couple of these storms ended up resulting in several downed trees. Multiple rounds of heavy rain moved across portions of Pike County, leading to a flash flood near the community of Mouthcard.
episodes.171452: After several rounds of showers and thunderstorms overnight on July 17th, Duck Creek rose above its banks in Washington County. This resulted in minor flooding before the creek returned to its banks.
episodes.171711: SW steering flow focused the sea breeze merger toward the Atlantic coast in the afternoon and evening where strong storms moved offshore and produced gusty winds that impacted the nearshore Atlantic waters.
episodes.171797: A strong cold front moved through the region triggering showers and storms. Some of the storms became severe producing damaging winds.
episodes.171802: In the morning, scattered showers developed across the Atlantic coastal waters along the land breeze. One of these showers produced a waterspout around sunrise off the southeast South Carolina coast. In the early afternoon, thunderstorms developed along the southeast Georgia coast and pushed out across the coastal waters, producing strong wind gusts.
episodes.171967: Two cold fronts swept across Arkansas bringing several rounds of severe thunderstorms to the region.
episodes.171989: There was video evidence of a waterspout on the Hudson River on July 18.
episodes.172205: A supercell thunderstorm moved from Saskatchewan into far northwest North Dakota. Wind gusts of 60 mph and ping pong ball size hail were reported in Divide County with this storm.
episodes.172282: Another day of afternoon and evening scattered shower and thunderstorm development was observed on this day. While most of the activity stayed below severe limits, there was an isolated severe storm that developed along the I-25 corridor and produced large hail just south of Trinidad.
episodes.172326: An upper level storm system passing to our north, combined with afternoon instability and marginal shear allowed for a few severe storms to form and produce localized damaging winds.
episodes.172327: An upper level storm system passing to our north, combined with afternoon instability and marginal shear allowed for a few severe storms to form and produce localized damaging winds.
episodes.172366: A mesoscale convective system moved from southeastern Missouri into western Kentucky during the late evening hours of July 17th. A combination of modest instability and shear (1500 J/kg MLCAPE; 30 knots effective shear) along with the dynamics of the MCS itself helped to sustain convection well after sunset as the system approached the Natcher Parkway. In addition to heavy rainfall and lightning, a few reports of wind damage were observed in Ohio County.
episodes.172456: Mid-level flow of 25-30 kts and divergence aloft combined with sufficient MLCAPE of  greater than 1000 J/kg to result in an environment favorable for the development of organized severe thunderstorms. A cluster of thunderstorms developed across southeast Pinal County during the late afternoon hours and moved northwestward through the Phoenix Metro after dark while becoming severe in the process. One of the more significant damage areas was along SR-87 in Salt River Reservation Community, where a mobile home and trailer park were destroyed and large transmission lines were downed. Power was knocked out for some for more than 2 days. A large dust storm also impacted parts of Pinal County.
episodes.172459: Deep moisture, light winds, and clear conditions in the morning allowed thunderstorms to produce heavy rain, flash flooding, and severe hail.
episodes.172471: Showers and storms developed during the afternoon across northwest Illinois. Four funnel clouds were reported with showers and storms near a boundary as it moved across the area during the afternoon hours.
episodes.172477: An upper level trough approaches from the west along with associated weak surface low pressure. The surface low passed to the north and west, but dragged a warm front and cold front through the waters. A round of severe thunderstorms moved through the waters in the morning hours with the warm front. Another round of severe thunderstorms moved through in the afternoon ahead of the cold front along a pre-frontal trough.
episodes.172483: An upper level trough approaches from the west along with associated weak surface low pressure. The surface low passed to the north and west, but dragged a warm front and cold front through northeast NJ. A round of severe thunderstorms moved through in the afternoon ahead of the cold front along a pre-frontal trough.
episodes.172557: A line of storms tracked from west to east through East Tennessee during the afternoon. A few stronger storms embedded in this line produced some isolated wind damage.
episodes.172558: A line of storms tracked from west to east through extreme southwest Virginia during the late afternoon. A few stronger storms embedded in this line produced some isolated wind damage.
episodes.172627: Another active setup in mid-late July resulted in numerous microburst related wind gusts in portions of Utah's West Desert Region, as well as a report of severe hail. Additionally, flash flooding was noted in southern Utah. This also coincided with a period of anomalous heat across much of the region.
episodes.172680: Scattered thunderstorms moved northwest across Pinal and Pima counties during the afternoon and evening. Storms became severe across southeast Pinal County where numerous power poles were downed that resulted a days long power outage. A dust storm caused a traffic accident on Interstate 10.
episodes.172758: Several rounds of heavy thunderstorms developed in the warm sector of a frontal system on July 18th, 2022. These thunderstorms developed in an environment with 2 to 2.3 inch PWAT values and CAPE near 3000 J/kg. Training thunderstorms produced a widespread 1 to 3 inches of rainfall with localized spots up to 4 inches.
episodes.172759: Several rounds of heavy thunderstorms developed in the warm sector of a frontal system on July 18th, 2022. These thunderstorms developed in an environment with 2 to 2.3 inch PWAT values and CAPE near 3000 J/kg. Training thunderstorms produced a widespread 1 to 3 inches of rainfall with localized spots up to 4 to 5 inches.

episodes.172816: Isolated severe thunderstorms formed near Lake of the Woods during the overnight hours, producing large hail and severe wind gusts.
episodes.172886: A push of monsoon moisture fueled an outbreak of thunderstorms across the Mojave Desert. Some storms produced severe weather and flash flooding.

SR-87 was closed between Loop-202 and Shea Blvd due to widespread wind damage. One mobile home and one modular home were destroyed resulting in one injury, requiring the person to be transported to the hospital and be placed in the Intensive Care Unit. Numerous power poles were blown down as well as several transmission towers that had collapsed. The transmission towers were in an area west of Gilbert Rd and along Highway 87. Salt River Project (SRP) utilities confirmed a total of 16 power poles were either blown over or snapped. They also confirmed another 5 (230 volt) transmission towers had collapsed. Other less severe damage was widespread across the region that included shingles blown off numerous homes, tree damage and damage to road signs. 20 other homes were listed as inhabitable. Initial wind estimates from NWS Phoenix were 80-100 mph. SRP rated their transmission towers for 90-95 mph. So, speeds may have actually been 100+ mph.

The tornado touched down 5.5 miles southwest of Glentana at 5:47 PM MDT, moving to the northeast and directly impacting the town of Glentana at 5:53 MDT.  Several blue spruce trees were uprooted, several grain hopper bins and some garages and farm machine buildings were destroyed.  The roof from a house was blown off.  The Glentana Hall metal roof peeled off on the south side.  Multiple farm machinery equipment were damaged.  Some straight line wind damage including one dozen power poles snapped, was observed 0.5 miles south of the path of the tornado on South Glentana Road.  The tornado continued toward the northeast and lifted at 5:56 PM MDT, 2.4 miles northeast of Glentana.
